title: Sebastian and the Confession
premise: Astrid Underhill, a retired detective who fled a career-ending scandal, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a decade-old drowning he helped bury in the official record, and one promising that 'the witness is still breathing.' As Astrid investigates, he discovers the confession was written by someone who knows his own hidden role in covering up the death of a young woman named Cora Vane. The trail leads through the town's most respectable families to a witness everyone believes dead—Cora's sister, living under a new name and gathering proof against them all. In the end, Astrid must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and testifying to his own complicity; he chooses truth, surrendering his anonymity and his bookshop, but saving the witness's life.
about_author: Gideon Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent fifteen years covering coroner's inquests and municipal scandals before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about ordinary people trapped by the secrets of the places they call home.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Astrid Underhill opens his failing bookshop on a rain-gray morning and finds two letters: one confessing to Cora Vane's drowning ten years ago, one reading only 'The witness is still breathing. You have until the equinox.' His POV; dread reawakens instincts he thought retired. Emotional beat: the past knocking at a door he sealed shut.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Astrid rereads his private case files from his detective years, confirming he signed off on the accidental-drowning ruling despite doubts. Flashbacks reveal the pressure from Chief Bramholt. His POV; guilt surfaces as memory. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing he wasn't deceived—he chose not to look.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Hand
chapters.summary: Astrid analyzes the confession's handwriting and paper, recognizing the fountain pen ink as the kind sold only at the pharmacy owned by Aldous Merrick, the town's beloved doctor. His POV; methodical hope. Emotional beat: the first thread pulled from a very old knot.

chapters.title: Tea with the Widow Vane
chapters.summary: Astrid visits Cora's mother, Edith, who has never accepted the ruling and keeps her daughter's room untouched. She mentions Cora had a half-sister, Lark, presumed drowned abroad years later. Astrid's POV; grief shared across a tea table. Emotional beat: sorrow that hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Chief Bramholt's Warning
chapters.summary: Bramholt summons Astrid, all charm and menace, reminding him of the scandal that ended his career and hinting the letters could destroy what peace he has left. Astrid's POV; fear and defiance warring. Emotional beat: the corrupt machinery of power flexing, quietly.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives for Someone Else
chapters.summary: Pharmacist's widow Nell Merrick finds an identical letter among her late husband's papers and brings it to Astrid, terrified. The confessions are copies—the original writer sent many. Astrid's POV; the mystery widens. Emotional beat: realization that someone is detonating the town's secrets systematically.

chapters.title: What Aldous Knew
chapters.summary: Searching Merrick's closed pharmacy, Astrid finds prescription records showing Cora was pregnant the summer she died—and that Bramholt's son Daniel was the father. Astrid's POV; cold fury. Emotional beat: motive crystallizing around a family's reputation.

chapters.title: Daniel Comes Home
chapters.summary: Daniel Bramholt returns to town after a decade away, polished and political, announcing a run for regional office. He visits the bookshop, probing Astrid with friendly menace. Alternating POV with brief Daniel section revealing he received a letter too. Emotional beat: predator recognizing predator.

chapters.title: The Drowned Girl Who Wrote Letters
chapters.summary: Astrid traces 'Lark' through ferry manifests and discovers she didn't drown—she changed her name and has been sending anonymous tips to a journalist for years. His POV; cautious exhilaration. Emotional beat: hope, dangerous and unfamiliar.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: The bookshop is broken into; his case files are gone, replaced by a single matchbook from the lakeside lodge where Cora died. Astrid's POV; violation and terror. Emotional beat: the investigation now has him in its sights.

chapters.title: The Lodge at Low Season
chapters.summary: Astrid revisits the shuttered lodge and reconstructs the night Cora died: a party, a boathouse, three sets of footprints in his old notes that were never followed up. His POV; forensic clarity. Emotional beat: the detective he buried rising from the files.

chapters.title: Nell's Confession
chapters.summary: Nell admits Aldous falsified the autopsy at Bramholt's request to protect Daniel, and that Aldous's guilt drove his final years. She gives Astrid Aldous's hidden ledger. Her POV chapter; relief and ruin intertwined. Emotional beat: complicity confessed at last.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: The ledger records payments from Bramholt senior to Aldous, the coroner, and—to Astrid's shame—a discreet sum to himself, framed as 'consulting fees' he never questioned. Astrid's POV; self-loathing. Emotional beat: discovering his own name in the corruption.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: With one day left before the letter's deadline, Astrid decodes the sender's return address pattern: mail drops from the coastal village of Greyhaven. He drives through fog, aware he may be walking into a trap. His POV; grim determination. Emotional beat: crossing the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Woman Called Lark
chapters.summary: In Greyhaven, Astrid meets Lark Vane—alive, sharp, and armed with recordings. She confesses she sent the letters to force the town open before Daniel's campaign makes it impossible. Dual POV; wary alliance forms. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Really Happened
chapters.summary: Lark reveals she witnessed the boathouse struggle as a teenager: Daniel pushed Cora during a confrontation over the pregnancy, and her parents paid to erase both girls—one dead, one exiled. Lark's POV; trauma narrated with terrible calm. Emotional beat: the full weight of the truth finally spoken.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Bramholt senior intercepts Astrid, offering reinstatement, money, and silence—revealing he's known where Lark lives for years. Astrid pretends to consider. His POV; controlled revulsion. Emotional beat: temptation offered by a man who thinks everyone has a price.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Astrid and Lark set their own trap: they let Daniel believe Lark will sell her testimony, luring him to a recorded meeting at the lodge. Tense alternating POV as the meeting teeters. Emotional beat: the hunted becoming hunters.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: Daniel, unmasked and desperate, turns violent; Bramholt senior arrives to contain the damage. In the struggle, Astrid takes a blow shielding Lark, while his recorder captures everything—including the chief threatening his own son. Multi-POV chaos. Climax. Emotional beat: violence echoing the original sin.

chapters.title: Arrests at Dawn
chapters.summary: State police, tipped by the journalist Lark fed for years, arrive with warrants. Daniel is charged; Bramholt senior resigns under investigation. Astrid gives a full statement, including his own cover-up. His POV; exhausted clarity. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: At the reopened inquest, Astrid testifies to what he ignored ten years ago, dismantling his own reputation to corroborate Lark. Public disgrace follows; the bookshop's lease is lost. His POV; grief and strange lightness. Emotional beat: paying the price of survival finally come due.

chapters.title: Shelf Life
chapters.summary: Months later, Astrid works in Lark's rebuilt Greyhaven bookshop-café, anonymous no longer but unburdened. Edith Vane visits, thanking him for giving Cora back her name. Final image: shelving a novel titled after the case. His POV; quiet redemption. Emotional beat: memory honored instead of filed away.
